Global mode
Install Astryx once on your computer and use it in any folder. Each project still runs its own version of Astryx, so a
global install never changes what a project gets.

package: @astryxdesign/cli

Global mode means installing the Astryx CLI once for your computer, so the astryx command works everywhere: in your
projects, in an empty folder, and for every coding agent. Inside a project, the project's own version of Astryx answers,
so your global install never changes what a project gets.

```bash
npm install -g @astryxdesign/cli
```

### What you get

- Docs, components, templates, and search in any folder, before you have a project.
- Every coding agent on your computer knows Astryx, through a short guide the CLI keeps where agent tools look.
- Each project keeps its own version: in a project, the project's version answers, whichever astryx command you run.

### Which version runs

Where you run it                                                               | Which version answers                                                                                                                              
------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Inside a project                                                               | The project's own CLI. In a project that installs only `@astryxdesign/core`, the astryx command you started, with a hint once a day to add the CLI.
Outside any project                                                            | Your global version.                                                                                                                               
Commands for your computer, such as `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 init --user` | Your global version, in any folder.                                                                                                                

Not sure whether you want a project install, a global one, or both: `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs
global/project-global-or-both`. The details: `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs global/who-answers`.

### Updates

Your global install never upgrades itself or a project. When a newer version is out, a command that succeeds ends with a
two-line notice, at most once a day: `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs global/updates`.

### Agents

The CLI keeps a short Astryx guide where agent tools look in your home folder, so an agent working anywhere knows Astryx
is there: `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs global/computer-agent-guide`.

### Integrations

Integrations you install next to your global install work outside projects. Inside a project, only the project's own
integrations do: `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs global/computer-integrations`. Building one: `npx
@astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs authoring/global-integrations`.

### More

- Install, and work offline: `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs global/install-once`.
- Monorepos and nested folders: `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs global/monorepos`.
- CI and containers: `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs global/ci-and-containers`.
- Something looks wrong: `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs global/problems`.
- Uninstall and reset: `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs global/uninstall`.
- Every path, setting, JSON field, and error code: `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs global/reference`.
- What each command does outside a project: `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs cli/commands`.

Global mode, question by question

project-global-or-both  Install Astryx in each project and once for your computer: both is the recommended setup, and
                        the two never conflict. What each side gives you, and how to set it up.
install-once            Install the Astryx CLI once for your computer with npm, pnpm, Yarn, Bun, or Volta, and what
                        happens when you are offline.
who-answers             Inside a project, the project's own CLI answers, whichever astryx command you start; in a
                        project with only Core, the astryx command you started answers. Outside a project, your global
                        install answers. How to see which one did.
updates                 Your global install checks for a newer version once a day and prints a two-line notice after a
                        command succeeds. It never upgrades itself or a project.
computer-agent-guide    Your global install keeps one short Astryx skill in your home folder and links it into the
                        folders agent tools read, so agents anywhere know Astryx is there. `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12
                        init --user` writes it now or turns it off.
computer-integrations   Integrations installed next to your global install work in folders outside any project. Inside a
                        project, only the integrations the project installs work, and the others are listed as ones you
                        could add.
monorepos               How Astryx finds the project a folder belongs to, and which version answers in a monorepo, a
                        nested app, or a cloned repository inside another project.
ci-and-containers       What Astryx does in CI and containers: no update checks or notices, the project's version as
                        always, and how to cache versions or work with a read-only home folder.
problems                Every line Astryx prints in global mode, what it means, and what to do. Plus the install
                        problems package managers cause: permissions, PATH, Corepack, and Windows.
uninstall               Remove your global install, the agent guide it keeps, and the folders it uses, or reset them to
                        start over.
reference               Every folder global mode uses on each system, the environment variables it reads, the JSON
                        fields it adds, its error codes, and a short glossary.

Open one: npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs global/<name>
Up: npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs
